source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: the last part of the book begins
decisions.reason: Chapters 25-32 were messages against the nations. Chapter 33 turns back to Israel and opens the book's last part, the messages of hope (chapters 33-48). It begins by giving Ezekiel his charge as a watchman again (verses 1-9), and then tells of the news that Jerusalem has fallen (verse 21).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶל־בְּנֵֽי־עַמְּךָ֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶ֕רֶץ כִּֽי־אָבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ חָ֑רֶב וְלָקְח֨וּ עַם־הָאָ֜רֶץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ מִקְצֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ לָהֶ֖ם לְצֹפֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, speak to [the] sons of your people and say to them: A land, when I bring on it a sword, and take [the] people of the land a man, one from their borders, and set him for them as a watchman,

en.L: Son of man, speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of your people and say to them, [Suppose there is] a land, when I bring a sword upon it, and the people of the land take one man from among them and set him as their watchman,
en.B: Son of man, speak to your own people and say to them, Suppose I bring the sword on some land, and its people pick one of their number and make him their watchman,
en.R: Son of man, speak to your own people. Tell them, Suppose I send war against a country. The people of that country choose one of their men to be their watchman.

decisions.choice: a watchman: a lookout who warns the city of danger
decisions.reason: See 3:17. The watchman stood on the wall or a tower and sounded the alarm when he saw an enemy coming. Here the LORD first describes an ordinary watchman chosen by his people (verses 2-6), and then applies the picture to Ezekiel (verses 7-9).

decisions.choice: a land, when I bring a sword upon it: a case set out for the hearers to judge
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with "a land" and then describes what happens to it, as a case in law is set out (compare 14:13). The sword is war: the enemy army that the LORD brings as judgment.

decisions.choice: from their borders: from among them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "from their ends" or "from their borders", that is, from among all the people of the land, wherever they live. It does not mean a stranger from the edge of the country.

decisions.choice: [Suppose there is] a land (L); Suppose (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with the bare words "a land", as in a case at law. Literal brackets the words English needs; Balanced and Readable say "Suppose". Literal gives "children" through the gender setting, and Balanced and Readable say "your own people", as at 3:11. The message Ezekiel is to give takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: וְרָאָ֥ה אֶת־הַחֶ֖רֶב בָּאָ֣ה עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְתָקַ֥ע בַּשּׁוֹפָ֖ר וְהִזְהִ֥יר אֶת־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and he sees the sword coming on the land and blows on [the] horn and warns the people,

en.L: and he sees the sword coming upon the land and blows the trumpet and warns the people,
en.B: and he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the ram's horn to warn the people.
en.R: The watchman sees the enemy army coming against the country. So he blows the trumpet to warn the people.

decisions.choice: the horn: the ram's horn used to sound an alarm
decisions.reason: The *shofar* was a ram's horn. Its blast warned a town that an enemy was coming (Jeremiah 4:5; 6:1; Amos 3:6).

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *shofar* in the prophets. Readable says "the enemy army" for the sword. The sentence runs on into verse 4 at Literal.

source.text: וְשָׁמַ֨ע הַשֹּׁמֵ֜עַ אֶת־ק֤וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר֙ וְלֹ֣א נִזְהָ֔ר וַתָּ֥בוֹא חֶ֖רֶב וַתִּקָּחֵ֑הוּ דָּמ֥וֹ בְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ יִֽהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and hears the hearer the sound of the horn and does not take warning, and comes [the] sword and takes him, his blood on his head will be.

en.L: then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and does not take warning, and the sword comes and takes {{gender:them|him}} away, {{gender:their|his}} blood will be on {{gender:their|his}} own head.
en.B: If anyone hears the sound of the horn but does not take the warning, and the sword comes and takes {{gender:them|him}} away, {{gender:their|his}} blood will be on {{gender:their|his}} own head.
en.R: Then anyone who hears the trumpet but does not pay attention to the warning will be to blame for {{gender:their|his}} own death when the enemy comes and kills {{gender:them|him}}.

decisions.choice: his blood will be on his head: he is to blame for his own death
decisions.reason: To have one's blood on one's own head is to be responsible for one's own death; no one else is guilty of it (Joshua 2:19; 2 Samuel 1:16).

decisions.choice: them, their / him, his (gender setting)
decisions.reason: Anyone who hears the alarm, man or woman, is meant, so the pronouns take the gender setting, as in 3:18-21, which this passage repeats. Readable gives the meaning of the idiom (m1).

source.text: אֵת֩ ק֨וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֤ר שָׁמַע֙ וְלֹ֣א נִזְהָ֔ר דָּמ֖וֹ בּ֣וֹ יִֽהְיֶ֑ה וְה֥וּא נִזְהָ֖ר נַפְשׁ֥וֹ מִלֵּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: The sound of the horn he heard and did not take warning; his blood on him will be. But he, [if he] had taken warning, his life he would have delivered.

en.L: {{gender:They|He}} heard the sound of the trumpet and did not take warning; {{gender:their|his}} blood will be upon {{gender:them|him}}. But if {{gender:they|he}} had taken warning, {{gender:they|he}} would have delivered {{gender:their|his}} life.
en.B: {{gender:They|He}} heard the sound of the horn but did not take the warning, so {{gender:their|his}} blood will be on {{gender:them|him}}. If {{gender:they|he}} had taken the warning, {{gender:they|he}} would have saved {{gender:their|his}} life.
en.R: {{gender:They|He}} heard the trumpet but did not pay attention, so it is {{gender:their|his}} own fault. If {{gender:they|he}} had paid attention, {{gender:they|he}} would have saved {{gender:their|his}} life.

decisions.choice: but he, had he taken warning, would have saved his life
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short: "and he, warned, his life he delivered". It describes what would have happened if he had listened. The warning gave him every chance.

decisions.choice: they, their / he, his (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

source.text: וְ֠הַצֹּפֶה כִּֽי־יִרְאֶ֨ה אֶת־הַחֶ֜רֶב בָּאָ֗ה וְלֹֽא־תָקַ֤ע בַּשּׁוֹפָר֙ וְהָעָ֣ם לֹֽא־נִזְהָ֔ר וַתָּב֣וֹא חֶ֔רֶב וַתִּקַּ֥ח מֵהֶ֖ם נָ֑פֶשׁ ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ נִלְקָ֔ח וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיַּֽד־הַצֹּפֶ֥ה אֶדְרֹֽשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But the watchman, if he sees the sword coming and does not blow on [the] horn, and the people are not warned, and comes [the] sword and takes from them a person, he in his iniquity is taken, but his blood from [the] hand of the watchman I will require.

en.L: But the watchman, if he sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet, and the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes a person from among them, that one is taken away in {{gender:their|his}} iniquity, but {{gender:their|his}} blood I will require from the watchman's hand.
en.B: But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes the life of any one of them, that person is taken away for {{gender:their|his}} sin, but I will hold the watchman responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.
en.R: But suppose the watchman sees the enemy coming and does not blow the trumpet. The people are not warned, and the enemy comes and kills one of them. That person dies because of {{gender:their|his}} own sin. But I will hold the watchman responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.

decisions.choice: his blood I will require from the watchman's hand: I will hold the watchman responsible
decisions.reason: As in 3:18, to require someone's blood is to call them to account for a death. The person still dies for their own sin, but the silent watchman shares the guilt.

decisions.choice: he is taken away in his iniquity: the one who dies is not innocent
decisions.reason: The picture of the watchman now begins to be applied to Ezekiel. The sword is the LORD's judgment, and those it takes are taken for their own sin (verses 8-9); the question is only whether they were warned.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); sin (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *'awon*, as in 3:18. Balanced and Readable say "hold responsible" for the idiom in m1, as in 3:18. The pronouns take the gender setting, as in verse 4.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֔ם צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֤ מִפִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר וְהִזְהַרְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, a watchman I have made you for [the] house of Israel; and you will hear from my mouth a word and warn them from me.

en.L: And you, son of man, a watchman I have made you for the house of Israel; and you will hear a word from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth and warn them from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: As for you, son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth, you must warn them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel. Whenever you hear a message from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you must warn them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: I have made you a watchman: the charge of 3:17-19 given again
decisions.reason: Verses 7-9 repeat the LORD's charge to Ezekiel in 3:17-19 almost word for word. It was given at the start of his work, when his message was judgment; it is given again now, as the news of Jerusalem's fall is about to arrive (verse 21) and his message turns to hope. The watchman's task is the same in both.

decisions.choice: the wording of 3:17 at each level
decisions.reason: Verses 7-9 reuse the published wording of 3:17-19 at each level wherever the Hebrew is the same. Here the Hebrew adds "And you" at the start, which Literal keeps and Balanced gives as "As for you". The LORD's message takes no quotation marks, here as in 3:17-21, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: בְּאָמְרִ֣י לָרָשָׁ֗ע רָשָׁע֙ מ֣וֹת תָּמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א דִבַּ֔רְתָּ לְהַזְהִ֥יר רָשָׁ֖ע מִדַּרְכּ֑וֹ ה֤וּא רָשָׁע֙ בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: When I say to the wicked, Wicked [one], surely you will die, and you do not speak to warn [the] wicked from his way, he, [the] wicked, in his iniquity will die, but his blood from your hand I will require.

en.L: When I say to the wicked, "Wicked [one], you will surely die," and you do not speak to warn the wicked from {{gender:their|his}} way, that wicked [person] will die for {{gender:their|his}} iniquity, but {{gender:their|his}} blood I will require from your hand.
en.B: If I say to a wicked person, "Wicked one, you will surely die," and you do not speak out to turn {{gender:them|him}} from {{gender:their|his}} way, that wicked person will die for {{gender:their|his}} sin, but I will hold you responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.
en.R: Suppose I tell a wicked person, "You wicked person, you will certainly die." If you do not warn {{gender:them|him}} to turn from {{gender:their|his}} ways, that wicked person will die because of {{gender:their|his}} sin. But I will hold you responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.

decisions.choice: the same words as 3:18, shortened
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 3:18. It adds the address "wicked one" before the sentence and leaves out the words "to keep him alive". The meaning is the same: a watchman who keeps silent shares the guilt for the death that follows.

decisions.choice: you will surely die: death in the coming judgment
decisions.reason: As in 3:18, the doubled verb is the form of a death sentence. Here it is death in the judgment the LORD brings, the sword of verses 2-6.

decisions.choice: the wording of 3:18 at each level, with "Wicked one"
decisions.reason: The wording of 3:18 is reused at each level, with the gender setting for the wicked person as there. Readable says "You wicked person" for the address. The words the LORD speaks to the wicked person take double quotation marks, as speech quoted inside the LORD's message.

source.text: וְ֠אַתָּה כִּֽי־הִזְהַ֨רְתָּ רָשָׁ֤ע מִדַּרְכּוֹ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְלֹא־שָׁ֖ב מִדַּרְכּ֑וֹ ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But you, if you warn [the] wicked from his way to turn from it, and he does not turn from his way, he in his iniquity will die, but you your life have delivered.

en.L: But you, if you warn the wicked [to turn] from {{gender:their|his}} way, to turn back from it, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not turn from {{gender:their|his}} way, {{gender:they|he}} will die for {{gender:their|his}} iniquity, but you will have delivered your life.
en.B: But if you warn the wicked to turn from {{gender:their|his}} way, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not turn from it, {{gender:they|he}} will die for {{gender:their|his}} sin, but you will have saved yourself.
en.R: But suppose you warn the wicked person to turn away from {{gender:their|his}} ways, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not turn away from them. Then {{gender:they|he}} will die because of {{gender:their|his}} sin, but you will have saved your own life.

decisions.choice: the same words as 3:19
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 3:19, with "his way" in place of "his wickedness and his wicked way". The watchman who gives the warning is free of guilt, whatever the hearer does.

decisions.choice: you will have delivered your life: you will have saved yourself
decisions.reason: As in 3:19, the word often translated "soul" means the life or self of the person.

decisions.choice: the wording of 3:19 at each level
decisions.reason: The wording of 3:19 is reused at each level, with the gender setting as there. Literal brackets "to turn", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood before "from his way".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹר֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֤ן אֲמַרְתֶּם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי־פְשָׁעֵ֥ינוּ וְחַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּבָ֛ם אֲנַ֥חְנוּ נְמַקִּ֖ים וְאֵ֥יךְ נִֽחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, say to [the] house of Israel: Thus you have said, saying, Our transgressions and our sins [are] on us, and in them we are rotting away; how then can we live?

en.L: And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, Thus you have said: "Our transgressions and our sins [are] upon us, and in them we are rotting away; how then can we live?"
en.B: As for you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, This is what you have been saying: "Our rebellious acts and our sins weigh on us, and we are wasting away because of them. How then can we live?"
en.R: Son of man, say to the people of Israel, You have been saying, "Our sins and our wrongs are crushing us. We are wasting away because of them. How can we go on living?"

decisions.choice: our sins are on us, and we are rotting away: the exiles' despair
decisions.reason: In chapter 18 the exiles complained that they were punished for their fathers' sins (18:2). Now they admit their own sins, but they think there is no hope left for them. The LORD answers that he wants them to turn and live (verse 11).

decisions.choice: we are rotting away in them: Leviticus 26:39 and Ezekiel 24:23
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:39 warns that those left in exile "will rot away in their iniquity". Ezekiel used the same verb in 24:23. The exiles now say that the warning has come true for them.

decisions.choice: transgressions (L); rebellious acts (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *pesha'* in Ezekiel, as in 18:22. Readable says "wrongs" for the second word so that the two do not repeat. The people's words take double quotation marks, as speech quoted inside the LORD's message.

source.text: אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי־אָ֣נִי׀נְאֻ֣ם׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם־אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם־בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Say to them: [As] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, I do not take pleasure in [the] death of the wicked, but in the turning of [the] wicked from his way, and he lives. Turn, turn from your ways, the evil; for why will you die, house of Israel?

en.L: Say to them, [As] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I do not delight in the death of the wicked, but in the wicked turning from his way and living. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why then will you die, house of Israel?
en.B: Tell them, As surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, the death of the wicked gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no pleasure. I would rather that they turn from their ways and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why would you die, house of Israel?
en.R: Tell them, As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I am not happy when evil people die. I want them to turn away from their evil ways and live. So turn back! Turn away from your evil ways! People of Israel, why should you die?

decisions.choice: I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked: 18:23 and 18:32 again
decisions.reason: The LORD's answer to their despair is the heart of chapter 18 (18:23, 32). Their past sins do not seal their fate: if they turn, they will live.

decisions.choice: as I live: the LORD's oath by his own life
decisions.reason: See 16:48. The LORD swears by his own life that he wants the wicked to live.

decisions.choice: turn back, turn back: the command doubled
decisions.reason: The doubled command makes the call urgent. The verb *shuv* means to turn around, to change direction (see 18:30).

decisions.choice: the wording of 18:23, 18:31 and 18:32
decisions.reason: The oath follows 16:48 ("As I live" / "As surely as I live"). The sentences about the LORD's pleasure and the closing question follow the published wording of 18:23, 18:31 and 18:32 at each level. Literal keeps the singular "his way" of the Hebrew; Balanced and Readable say "they", as in chapter 18.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹ֤ר אֶל־בְּנֵֽי־עַמְּךָ֙ צִדְקַ֣ת הַצַּדִּ֗יק לֹ֤א תַצִּילֶ֨נּוּ֙ בְּי֣וֹם פִּשְׁע֔וֹ וְרִשְׁעַ֤ת הָֽרָשָׁע֙ לֹֽא־יִכָּ֣שֶׁל בָּ֔הּ בְּי֖וֹם שׁוּב֣וֹ מֵֽרִשְׁע֑וֹ וְצַדִּ֗יק לֹ֥א יוּכַ֛ל לִֽחְי֥וֹת בָּ֖הּ בְּי֥וֹם חֲטֹאתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, say to [the] sons of your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not deliver him on [the] day of his transgression; and the wickedness of the wicked, he will not stumble by it on [the] day of his turning from his wickedness; and the righteous will not be able to live by it on [the] day of his sinning.

en.L: And you, son of man, say to the {{gender:children|sons}} of your people, The righteousness of the righteous [person] will not deliver him on the day of his transgression; and the wickedness of the wicked [person], he will not stumble by it on the day he turns from his wickedness; and the righteous will not be able to live by his [righteousness] on the day he sins.
en.B: As for you, son of man, say to your own people, The righteousness of righteous people will not save them when they rebel. And the wickedness of wicked people will not bring them down when they turn from their wickedness. Righteous people will not be able to live by their righteousness when they sin.
en.R: Son of man, say to your own people, If good people start to sin, the good they have done will not save them. And if evil people turn away from their evil, the evil they have done will not destroy them. If good people sin, they will not live because of the good they did before.

decisions.choice: the teaching of 18:21-28
decisions.reason: Verses 12-20 restate the teaching of chapter 18 in short form: each person is judged by the way they are now living, not by their past. A righteous person who turns to sin cannot rely on past goodness (18:24), and a wicked person who turns from sin is not held to the past (18:21-22).

decisions.choice: he will not stumble by it: his past wickedness will not bring him down
decisions.reason: To stumble is to fall under judgment (compare "a stumbling block of iniquity", 18:30). The wicked person who turns will not be brought down by the wickedness they have left behind.

decisions.choice: righteous people ... them; wicked people ... them
decisions.reason: As in 18:21-28, the Hebrew uses "he" for any person. Literal keeps the singular "he" of the Hebrew; Balanced and Readable use "people" and "they", which include everyone, as the Hebrew means. This follows chapter 18, which these verses repeat; verses 4-9, which repeat 3:17-21, keep that passage's gender setting instead.

decisions.choice: good people ... evil people (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "good" and "evil" for "righteous" and "wicked", as in 18:24-27. Literal brackets "righteousness", which the Hebrew gives only as "it".

source.text: בְּאָמְרִ֤י לַצַּדִּיק֙ חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְהֽוּא־בָטַ֥ח עַל־צִדְקָת֖וֹ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֑וֶל כָּל־צִדְקֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א תִזָּכַ֔רְנָה וּבְעַוְל֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה בּ֥וֹ יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: When I say to the righteous, Surely he will live, and he trusts in his righteousness and does injustice, all his righteous deeds will not be remembered; and in his injustice that he has done, in it he will die.

en.L: When I say to the righteous, "He will surely live," and he trusts in his righteousness and does injustice, none of his righteous deeds will be remembered; and for his injustice that he has done, for it he will die.
en.B: If I say that righteous people will surely live, but they trust in their own righteousness and do wrong, none of the righteous things they have done will be remembered. Because of the wrong they have done, they will die.
en.R: Suppose I promise good people that they will certainly live. But then they trust in the good they have done and start doing wrong. None of the good things they did will be remembered. They will die because of the wrong things they have done.

decisions.choice: when I say to the righteous, "He will surely live"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to the righteous" and then speaks of him in the third person, "he will surely live". It is the LORD's promise about the righteous, the verdict given in 18:9.

decisions.choice: he trusts in his righteousness: relying on past goodness as a license to sin
decisions.reason: The danger is not righteousness but trusting in it, as if past goodness gave a right to do wrong. Compare 18:24.

decisions.choice: righteous people ... they
decisions.reason: As in verse 12. Balanced and Readable report the promise ("that righteous people will surely live") rather than quote it, since they use the plural. All his righteous deeds "will not be remembered" follows 18:24 at each level.

source.text: וּבְאָמְרִ֥י לָֽרָשָׁ֖ע מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת וְשָׁב֙ מֵֽחַטָּאת֔וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And when I say to the wicked, Surely you will die, and he turns from his sin and does justice and righteousness,

en.L: And when I say to the wicked, "You will surely die," and he turns back from his sin and does justice and righteousness,
en.B: Again, if I say to wicked people, "You will surely die," but they turn from their sin and do what is just and right,
en.R: Or suppose I tell evil people, "You will certainly die." But then they turn away from their sin and do what is fair and right.

decisions.choice: turns from his sin and does justice and righteousness: 18:21 and 18:27
decisions.reason: The words follow 18:21 and 18:27. The verse begins a case that runs on into verses 15-16.

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness (L); what is just and right (B); what is fair and right (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 18:5, 21 and 27 at each level. The sentence runs on into verse 15, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

source.text: חֲבֹ֨ל יָשִׁ֤יב רָשָׁע֙ גְּזֵלָ֣ה יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם בְּחֻקּ֤וֹת הַֽחַיִּים֙ הָלַ֔ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י עֲשׂ֣וֹת עָ֑וֶל חָי֥וֹ יִֽחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: [if the] wicked returns a pledge, repays robbery, in the statutes of life walks, not doing injustice, surely he will live; he will not die.

en.L: [if] the wicked restores a pledge, repays what he took by robbery, walks in the statutes of life, not doing injustice, he will surely live; he will not die.
en.B: if they return what was given them as a pledge, pay back what they have taken by robbery, and follow the statutes that give life, doing nothing wrong, they will surely live; they will not die.
en.R: They give back what was given them as a promise to pay back a loan. They pay back what they have stolen. They live by the laws that give life, and they do nothing wrong. Then they will certainly live. They will not die.

decisions.choice: returns a pledge, repays robbery: the deeds of 18:7
decisions.reason: The righteous man of 18:7 returns the debtor's pledge and commits no robbery. Here the wicked who turns makes good what he took wrongly (compare Leviticus 6:1-5).

decisions.choice: the statutes of life: the laws that lead to life
decisions.reason: The LORD's statutes are those by which a person "will live" (20:11; Leviticus 18:5).

decisions.choice: they
decisions.reason: As in verse 12. Readable explains the pledge as in 18:7.

source.text: כָּל־חַטֹּאתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א לֹ֥א תִזָּכַ֖רְנָה ל֑וֹ מִשְׁפָּ֧ט וּצְדָקָ֛ה עָשָׂ֖ה חָי֥וֹ יִֽחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: All his sins that he has sinned will not be remembered against him; justice and righteousness he has done; surely he will live.

en.L: All his sins that he has sinned will not be remembered against him; justice and righteousness he has done; he will surely live.
en.B: None of the sins they have committed will be remembered against them. They have done what is just and right; they will surely live.
en.R: None of the sins they have committed will be held against them. They have done what is fair and right, so they will certainly live.

decisions.choice: will not be remembered against him: will not be held against him
decisions.reason: As in 18:22, for God to "remember" sins is to act on them in judgment.

decisions.choice: the wording of 18:22 (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable reuse the wording of 18:22 for the first sentence, with "they", as there.

source.text: וְאָמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֔ לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י וְהֵ֖מָּה דַּרְכָּ֥ם לֹֽא־יִתָּכֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And say the sons of your people, Not right is the way of [the] Lord; but they, their way is not right.

en.L: Yet the {{gender:children|sons}} of your people say, "Not right is the way of the Lord," but [it is] they [whose] way is not right.
en.B: Yet your own people say, "The Lord's way is not fair." But it is their own way that is not fair.
en.R: But your people say, "What the Lord does is not fair." But it is what they do that is not fair.

decisions.choice: not right is the way of the Lord: the charge of 18:25 and 18:29
decisions.reason: The people say that the LORD's dealings do not measure up. The verb means to be weighed or measured, as in 18:25. The LORD turns the charge back on them.

decisions.choice: the wording of 18:25 at each level
decisions.reason: The people's words reuse the published wording of 18:25. "Lord" here translates *Adonai*.

source.text: בְּשׁוּב־צַדִּ֥יק מִצִּדְקָת֖וֹ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֑וֶל וּמֵ֖ת בָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: When turns [the] righteous from his righteousness and does injustice, he will die in them.

en.L: When the righteous turns from his righteousness and does injustice, he will die for them.
en.B: If righteous people turn away from their righteousness and do wrong, they will die for it.
en.R: If good people stop doing what is right and start doing wrong, they will die because of it.

decisions.choice: the same words as 18:26
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 18:26 in short form. "Them" are the wrongs he has done.

decisions.choice: righteous people ... they
decisions.reason: The wording of 18:26 at each level, with "people" and "they" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 12.

source.text: וּבְשׁ֤וּב רָשָׁע֙ מֵֽרִשְׁעָת֔וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם ה֥וּא יִֽחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And when turns [the] wicked from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, on [account of] them he will live.

en.L: And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness, because of them he will live.
en.B: And if wicked people turn away from their wickedness and do what is just and right, they will live because of it.
en.R: And if evil people stop doing evil and start doing what is fair and right, they will live because of it.

decisions.choice: the same words as 18:27
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 18:27, with "he will live" in place of "he will keep his soul alive".

decisions.choice: wicked people ... they
decisions.reason: The wording of 18:27 at each level, as in verse 12.

source.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י אִ֧ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֛יו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

records.literal_gloss: And you say, Not right is the way of [the] Lord. Each according to his ways I will judge you, house of Israel.

en.L: Yet you say, "Not right is the way of the Lord." I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways.
en.B: Yet you say, "The Lord's way is not fair." House of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways.
en.R: But you say, "What the Lord does is not fair." People of Israel, I will judge each of you by what you have done.

decisions.choice: each according to his ways I will judge you: 18:30
decisions.reason: The section ends as chapter 18 does (18:29-30): the LORD will judge each person by their own ways. This is fair, because each person is judged for what they themselves have done.

decisions.choice: the wording of 18:29-30 at each level
decisions.reason: The people's words reuse 18:29, and the LORD's answer reuses 18:30.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא־אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] twelfth year, in the tenth, on [the] fifth of the month, of our exile, came to me the fugitive from Jerusalem, saying, The city has been struck down.

en.L: And it came about in the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth [month], on the fifth of the month, [that] the fugitive from Jerusalem came to me, saying, "The city has been struck down!"
en.B: In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, a survivor who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has fallen!"
en.R: On the fifth day of the tenth month, in the twelfth year of our exile, someone who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me. He said, "The city has been captured!"

decisions.choice: the twelfth year of our exile, the tenth month, the fifth day: about January 585 BC
decisions.reason: Ezekiel counts the years from the exile of King Jehoiachin in 597 BC (1:2). By that reckoning the date falls about January 585 BC. Jerusalem fell in the fourth month of the eleventh year of King Zedekiah, in the summer of 586 BC (2 Kings 25:2-4; Jeremiah 39:2), so the news reached the exiles about five or six months later, a reasonable time for the journey from Judah to Babylonia (Ezra 7:9 gives four months).

decisions.choice: the twelfth year: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: Some Hebrew manuscripts and some ancient translations, among them the Syriac and some Greek manuscripts, read "the eleventh year". That would bring the news only a few months after the fall. The standard Hebrew text, "the twelfth year", fits the date of the fall if the years of the exile are counted differently from the years of Zedekiah's reign, and it is kept.

decisions.choice: the fugitive from Jerusalem: the messenger promised in 24:26
decisions.reason: In 24:26-27 the LORD told Ezekiel that on the day the temple fell a fugitive would come to tell him, and that his mouth would then be opened. The article ("the fugitive") points back to that promise.

decisions.choice: the twelfth year of our exile (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "of our exile" at the end of the date. Each level moves it next to the year, following the wording of dated headings in Jeremiah ("in the Nth year of X"). Readable gives the day first, as at 1:1. The fugitive's words take double quotation marks, as the book's narrative quotes speech.

source.text: וְיַד־יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בָּעֶ֗רֶב לִפְנֵי֙ בּ֣וֹא הַפָּלִ֔יט וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח אֶת־פִּ֔י עַד־בּ֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיִּפָּ֣תַח פִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱלַ֖מְתִּי עֽוֹד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And the hand of Yahweh had been on me in the evening before the coming of the fugitive, and he opened my mouth until [he] came to me in the morning; and my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.

en.L: Now the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had been upon me in the evening before the fugitive came, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had opened my mouth by the time he came to me in the morning. Then my mouth was opened, and I was mute no longer.
en.B: The evening before the survivor arrived, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had opened my mouth by the time the man reached me the next morning. My mouth was opened, and I was silent no more.
en.R: The evening before the man arrived, the power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me. By the time the man came to me the next morning, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made me able to speak again. My mouth was opened, and I was no longer unable to speak.

decisions.choice: my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute: the end of the silence of 3:26-27
decisions.reason: At his call the LORD made Ezekiel unable to speak, except when the LORD gave him a message (3:26-27), and in 24:27 he promised that Ezekiel's mouth would be opened when the news of the fall arrived. The verse says it happened. From now on Ezekiel speaks freely, and his message turns to hope.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD had been on me: the LORD's power took hold of me
decisions.reason: See 1:3. Here the LORD's hand prepares Ezekiel for the news before it comes.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD had been upon me (L); had come on me (B); the power of the LORD came on me (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Ezekiel, with the past perfect for the Hebrew's order. Readable says "made me able to speak again" for the opening of the mouth, and names the LORD in place of "he", for clarity.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהֹוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: a new message
decisions.reason: A message about the people left in the ruined land of Judah (verses 24-29).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם יֹ֠שְׁבֵי הֶחֳרָב֨וֹת הָאֵ֜לֶּה עַל־אַדְמַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֹמְרִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר אֶחָד֙ הָיָ֣ה אַבְרָהָ֔ם וַיִּירַ֖שׁ אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ רַבִּ֔ים לָ֛נוּ נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, the inhabitants of these ruins on [the] soil of Israel are saying, saying, One was Abraham, and he possessed the land; but we [are] many; to us is given the land as a possession.

en.L: Son of man, those who live in these ruins on the soil of Israel are saying, "Abraham was [only] one [man], and he possessed the land; but we [are] many; the land has been given to us as a possession."
en.B: Son of man, the people who live among those ruins in Israel keep saying, "Abraham was just one man, and yet the land became his. But there are many of us. The land has surely been given to us to possess."
en.R: Son of man, the people who are living among the ruins in Israel keep saying, "Abraham was just one man, and the land was given to him. There are many of us, so the land must belong to us now."

decisions.choice: Abraham was one, and he possessed the land: Isaiah 51:2
decisions.reason: The LORD gave the land to Abraham and his descendants (Genesis 15:7; 17:8). Isaiah 51:2 also points to Abraham as one man whom the LORD blessed and made many, but to give hope to the humble. Here the survivors use him to claim the land for themselves, as those in Jerusalem had claimed it against the exiles (11:15).

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of these ruins: those left in Judah after the fall
decisions.reason: After Jerusalem fell, the Babylonians left some of the poor in the land (2 Kings 25:12; Jeremiah 39:10). They claimed the land of those who had been taken away.

decisions.choice: [only] one [man] (L); only one man (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "one was Abraham". The point is that he was one man and they are many, so each level says "only one man". The people's words take double quotation marks, as speech quoted inside the LORD's message.

source.text: לָכֵן֩ אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה עַל־הַדָּ֧ם׀תֹּאכֵ֛לוּ וְעֵינֵכֶ֛ם תִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶל־גִּלּוּלֵיכֶ֖ם וְדָ֣ם תִּשְׁפֹּ֑כוּ וְהָאָ֖רֶץ תִּירָֽשׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore say to them: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: With the blood you eat, and your eyes you lift to your idols, and blood you shed; and the land will you possess?

en.L: Therefore say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: You eat [meat] with the blood, and lift up your eyes to your filthy idols, and shed blood; and will you possess the land?
en.B: Therefore say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: You eat meat with the blood still in it, look to your idols and shed blood. And you expect to possess the land?
en.R: So tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You eat meat that still has blood in it. You look to your idols for help, and you murder people. Do you really think the land should belong to you?

decisions.choice: you eat with the blood: eating meat that has not been drained of its blood
decisions.reason: The Law forbade eating meat with its blood still in it, because the life is in the blood (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:10-14; 19:26). The phrase may also point to eating at the shrines of other gods.

decisions.choice: lift your eyes to your idols: look to them in worship and for help
decisions.reason: See 18:6. The idols are *gillulim* (see 6:4).

decisions.choice: will you possess the land?: the land is not theirs by right while they break the covenant
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no". The land was given on condition of faithfulness (Leviticus 18:24-28); people who do what the nations did before them cannot claim it.

decisions.choice: the formula as set at 2:4; filthy idols (L), idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "Thus says the Lord GOD" and for *gillulim*. Literal brackets "meat", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood. Readable says "murder people" for "shed blood".

source.text: עֲמַדְתֶּ֤ם עַֽל־חַרְבְּכֶם֙ עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ן תּוֹעֵבָ֔ה וְאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ טִמֵּאתֶ֑ם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ תִּירָֽשׁוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: You stand on your sword, you commit abomination, and each the wife of his neighbor you defile; and the land will you possess?

en.L: You rely on your sword, you commit abomination, and each of you defiles his neighbor's wife; and will you possess the land?
en.B: You rely on your sword, you do detestable things, and each of you defiles his neighbor's wife. And you expect to possess the land?
en.R: You depend on your weapons. You do disgusting things. Men sleep with other men's wives. Do you really think the land should belong to you?

decisions.choice: you stand on your sword: you rely on violence
decisions.reason: To "stand on" something is to depend on it. They live by force, not by the LORD's law.

decisions.choice: you commit abomination: the verb is feminine
decisions.reason: The verb "you do" has an unusual feminine plural ending in the Hebrew, perhaps a scribal slip or an old form. The meaning is plain.

decisions.choice: abomination (L); detestable things (B); disgusting things (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *to'evah*. Literal follows the Hebrew's "and each" literally ("each of you defiles his neighbor's wife"); the act is a man's, so it takes no gender setting. Readable says plainly what "defile his neighbor's wife" means, as the register rule for Ezekiel sets out.

source.text: כֹּֽה־תֹאמַ֨ר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֮ חַי־אָנִי֒ אִם־לֹ֞א אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֶּֽחֳרָבוֹת֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לַחַיָּ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יו לְאָכְל֑וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֛ר בַּמְּצָד֥וֹת וּבַמְּעָר֖וֹת בַּדֶּ֥בֶר יָמֽוּתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus you will say to them: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: [As] I live, surely those in the ruins by the sword will fall, and whoever [is] on the face of the field to the beasts I will give him to eat him, and those in the strongholds and in the caves by pestilence will die.

en.L: Thus you will say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: [As] I live, surely those who are in the ruins will fall by the sword, and whoever is on the open field I will give to the beasts for food, and those in the fortresses and in the caves will die by pestilence.
en.B: Say this to them: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: As surely as I live, those who are in the ruins will fall by the sword, whoever is out in the open field I will give to the wild animals to be eaten, and those in the strongholds and caves will die of plague.
en.R: Tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: As surely as I live, the people living in the ruins will be killed in war. I will let wild animals eat those who are out in the fields. And those hiding in forts and caves will die of disease.

decisions.choice: sword, wild animals and pestilence: the judgments of 14:21
decisions.reason: The same judgments are named in 5:17 and 14:21 and in the covenant warnings of Leviticus 26:22-25. No place in the land will be safe: the ruins, the open country or the hiding places.

decisions.choice: as I live, surely: an oath
decisions.reason: The oath has the form "if not ...", which in Hebrew means "surely".

decisions.choice: pestilence (L); plague (B); disease (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set in Jeremiah for *deber* with the sword. The oath follows 16:48.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֣ה וּמְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְנִשְׁבַּ֖ת גְּא֣וֹן עֻזָּ֑הּ וְשָֽׁמְמ֛וּ הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֵ֥ין עוֹבֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make the land a desolation and a waste, and will cease the pride of her strength, and will be desolate [the] mountains of Israel, with none passing through.

en.L: And I will make the land a desolation and a waste, and the pride of its strength will cease, and the mountains of Israel will be desolate, with no one passing through.
en.B: I will make the land a desolate waste, and the strength it was so proud of will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will be so desolate that no one will travel through them.
en.R: I will make the land empty and ruined. The power it was so proud of will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will be so empty that no one will travel through them.

decisions.choice: a desolation and a waste; the pride of her strength: Leviticus 26:19, 33
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:19 warns, "I will break the pride of your power", and 26:33 that the land will be a desolation. The same words are used in 7:24 and 24:21.

decisions.choice: the strength it was so proud of (B); the power it was so proud of (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable unpack "the pride of its strength".

source.text: וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּתִתִּ֤י אֶת־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֣ה וּמְשַׁמָּ֔ה עַ֥ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲבֹתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I make the land a desolation and a waste because of all their abominations that they have done.

en.L: And they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I make the land a desolation and a waste because of all their abominations that they have committed.
en.B: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I make the land a desolate waste because of all the detestable things they have done.
en.R: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I make the land empty and ruined because of all the disgusting things they have done.

decisions.choice: they will know that I am the LORD: the book's refrain
decisions.reason: See 6:7. The judgment shows who the LORD is.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R); abominations / detestable things / disgusting things
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain and of *to'evah* in Ezekiel.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֔ם בְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ הַנִּדְבָּרִ֤ים בְּךָ֙ אֵ֣צֶל הַקִּיר֔וֹת וּבְפִתְחֵ֖י הַבָּתִּ֑ים וְדִבֶּר־חַ֣ד אֶת־אַחַ֗ד אִ֤ישׁ אֶת־אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֹּֽאוּ־נָ֣א וְשִׁמְע֔וּ מָ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר הַיּוֹצֵ֖א מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, the sons of your people who talk about you beside the walls and in the doorways of the houses, and speak one with another, each with his brother, saying, Come now and hear what [is] the word that comes out from Yahweh.

en.L: And you, son of man, the {{gender:children|sons}} of your people who talk about you by the walls and in the doorways of the houses speak to one another, each to his brother, saying, "Come now and hear what the word is that comes from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: As for you, son of man, your own people are talking about you beside the walls and in the doorways of their houses. They say to one another, "Come and hear what message has come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Son of man, your people are talking about you. They stand by the walls and in the doorways of their houses and say to each other, "Come on, let us go and hear the latest message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: talk about you: talk about Ezekiel, perhaps against him
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "talk about you" or "talk against you". The verses that follow suggest gossip and curiosity more than open hostility.

decisions.choice: beside the walls and in the doorways: the places where neighbors met and talked
decisions.reason: People gathered in the shade of the walls and at their doors to talk. Ezekiel's preaching has become the talk of the town.

decisions.choice: to one another (B); to each other (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "each to his brother"; Balanced and Readable give its sense. Readable says "the latest message" for the people's eager curiosity. Their words take double quotation marks, as speech quoted inside the LORD's message.

source.text: וְיָב֣וֹאוּ אֵ֠לֶיךָ כִּמְבוֹא־עָ֞ם וְיֵשְׁב֤וּ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ עַמִּ֔י וְשָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ וְאוֹתָ֖ם לֹ֣א יַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ כִּֽי־עֲגָבִ֤ים בְּפִיהֶם֙ הֵ֣מָּה עֹשִׂ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֥י בִצְעָ֖ם לִבָּ֥ם הֹלֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they come to you as people come, and sit before you [as] my people, and hear your words, but them they do not do; for love [songs] in their mouth they make, [but] after their gain their heart goes.

en.L: And they come to you as a people comes, and sit before you [as] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and hear your words, but they do not do them; for love [songs] they make with their mouth, [but] after their gain their heart goes.
en.B: They come to you as people usually do and sit in front of you as if they were {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. They hear your words, but they do not put them into practice. With their mouths they speak of love, but their hearts are set on gain.
en.R: They come to you in crowds and sit in front of you as if they were {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. They listen to what you say, but they do not do it. They talk about how much they love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but all they really want is to make money.

decisions.choice: love in their mouth they make: they speak warmly, but do not mean it
decisions.reason: The word *'agavim* means passionate love or love songs (compare verse 32). Here it seems to mean that their words are full of devotion while their hearts are elsewhere. The Septuagint reads "falsehood" in their mouth.

decisions.choice: their gain: unjust profit
decisions.reason: The word means profit gained wrongly (22:13, 27). Their real concern is money, not the LORD's word.

decisions.choice: as people come ... as my people: they look like true worshipers
decisions.reason: They come and sit before the prophet like a people eager to hear the LORD, as the elders did in 8:1 and 20:1. The words "my people" may mean they sit there as if they were the LORD's people.

decisions.choice: how much they love me; to make money
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the love on their lips and the gain in their hearts refer to (m1, m2). Literal brackets "as" and "but", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

source.text: וְהִנְּךָ֤ לָהֶם֙ כְּשִׁ֣יר עֲגָבִ֔ים יְפֵ֥ה ק֖וֹל וּמֵטִ֣ב נַגֵּ֑ן וְשָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ וְעֹשִׂ֥ים אֵינָ֖ם אוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, you [are] to them like a song of love, beautiful of voice and good at playing; and they hear your words, but they do not do them.

en.L: And look, you [are] to them like a love song, [sung by one] with a beautiful voice who plays well; and they hear your words, but they do not do them.
en.B: To them you are like someone who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays an instrument well. They hear your words, but they do not put them into practice.
en.R: To them you are just a singer who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays music well. They listen to your words, but they do not do what you say.

decisions.choice: like a love song, beautiful of voice and playing well: entertainment, not a message to obey
decisions.reason: The people enjoy Ezekiel's words as they would enjoy a good singer, but they do not act on them. Compare James 1:22-24.

decisions.choice: [sung by one] with a beautiful voice (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves from the song to the singer without a word between. Literal brackets the words English needs; Balanced and Readable compare Ezekiel to the singer.

source.text: וּבְבֹאָ֑הּ הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֔ה וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י נָבִ֖יא הָיָ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And when it comes, look, it is coming, they will know that a prophet has been among them.

en.L: But when it comes, and look, it is coming, they will know that a prophet has been among them.
en.B: But when all this comes true, and it surely will, they will know that a prophet has been among them.
en.R: But all this is going to happen. When it does, they will know that a prophet has been with them.

decisions.choice: they will know that a prophet has been among them: 2:5
decisions.reason: The LORD said at Ezekiel's call that whether they listened or not, they would know that a prophet had been among them (2:5). When his words come true, they will see that he spoke for the LORD (Deuteronomy 18:22).

decisions.choice: when it comes: when what the prophet says happens
decisions.reason: "It" is what Ezekiel announces. The fall of the city has proved his earlier words; the people will learn the same from the rest.

decisions.choice: when all this comes true, and it surely will (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "it" is, and give "look, it is coming" as a firm promise.
